title: India offers zero taxes through 2047 to lure global AI workloads
description: New Delhi's latest move comes as Amazon, Google, and Microsoft expand data center investments in India.
author: Jagmeet Singh

title: Bye-bye corporate conglomerates. Hello personal conglomerates.

author: Tim De Chant

title: Nvidia CEO pushes back against report that his company’s $100B OpenAI investment has stalled
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that a recent report of friction between his company and OpenAI was “nonsense.”
author: Anthony Ha

title: A peek inside Physical Intelligence, the startup building Silicon Valley’s buzziest robot brains
description: If co-founder Lachy Groom has any doubts, he doesn’t show it. He’s working with people who've been working on this problem for decades and who believe the timing is finally right, which is all he needs to know.
author: Connie Loizos

title: OpenClaw’s AI assistants are now building their own social network

title: Anthropic brings agentic plug-ins to Cowork
description: The company says you can use plug-ins to "tell Claude how you like work done, which tools and data to pull from, how to handle critical workflows, and what slash commands to expose so your team gets more consistent outcomes."

title: Last 24 hours to grab your plus-one pass at 50% off to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
description: Today is the last day to lock in a plus-one pass at 50% off to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, happening on October 13-15 in San Francisco.
author: TechCrunch Events

title: Guys, I don’t think Tim Cook knows how to monetize AI
description: One intrepid Morgan Stanley analyst dared to ask how Apple will make money on its AI investments. The answer will not shock you.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI in talks to merge, according to reports

title: Satya Nadella insists people are using Microsoft’s Copilot AI a lot

title: Apple buys Israeli startup Q.ai as the AI race heats up

title: Music publishers sue Anthropic for $3B over ‘flagrant piracy’ of 20,000 works
